source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: AR/company commentary describes diversified raw-material sourcing with reduced China dependence, solvent recovery-driven cost gains, and positions India (and Divi's peptide/CDMO/custom-synthesis business) as a 'trusted global manufacturing hub' benefiting from global supply-chain diversification; new 200-acre greenfield Phase I facility began production Jan 2025 to support backward integration.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: No formal derivative-hedging disclosure found; company appears to rely on natural/geographic diversification (multiple export markets - Europe, US) as a buffer against currency/tariff risk rather than financial hedges, per broker/industry commentary.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY24 export gross sales 87% of total; Europe 52.3% (vs 40.3% FY23), North America 17.1% (vs 28.9% FY23). Exact FY25 AR figures not directly retrieved (PDF fetch blocked).

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories appears on the Dept. of Pharmaceuticals' list of applicants approved under the PLI scheme for KSMs/Drug Intermediates/APIs (Category 2). No incentive amount or revenue attribution specific to Divi's disclosed in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: No specific rural revenue % disclosed. Royal Enfield is expanding Tier-2/3 reach via 'Studio Store' smaller-format outlets and partner workshops, and industry-wide two-wheeler demand commentary cites rural India as a key growth driver, but Eicher's own AR does not quantify a rural/semi-urban revenue split.

inr_exposure.evidence: Royal Enfield exports (100,136 units, +29.7% YoY) are ~10% of FY25 volumes, implying modest USD/other FX revenue exposure, but no explicit USD-revenue % or hedging policy was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors Limited is listed among companies approved under the 'Champion OEM Incentive' component of India's PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components (Ministry of Heavy Industries / PIB disclosures); VECV (Eicher's CV JV) is also developing hydrogen ICE tech under the PLI-Auto scheme. Revenue contribution from PLI-linked products not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Domestic-only diagnostics services company; no export business, no China+1 narrative found.

rural.evidence: Could not confirm an exact FY25-disclosed rural/semi-urban % from primary AR (PDF fetch blocked by host). Secondary/third-party sources indicate Tier-3+ towns contributed roughly 34% of revenue in FY23 rising toward ~39% by FY26, with company running a dedicated rural push branded 'GraminFit' and citing tier-2/3 hospital/household penetration (<20% organized-diagnostics penetration) as a growth target; FY25-specific figure not confirmed, so left null per no-invention rule.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI relevance found; diagnostics services company, not a manufacturer covered by pharma PLI schemes.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative found; company sources some inputs from China (per supply-chain data providers) alongside Italy and the US, but no diversification-away-from-China framing identified in disclosures reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 total revenue ~Rs 7,896 crore: Domestic Rs 3,660cr (46.4%, +16.4% YoY), International Rs 4,236cr (53.6%, +20.5% YoY) split into Emerging Markets Rs 1,510cr (19.1%, +27.9%), EU Rs 1,474cr (18.7%, +4.4%), Canada Rs 1,252cr (15.9%, +35.7%). Source: press release/earnings summary figures on emcure.com and financial media; primary AR PDF fetch was blocked (403).

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharmaceuticals is named among approved domestic applicants under the pharma PLI scheme (formulations/biopharmaceuticals/API category); no specific revenue or incentive amount disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Press coverage of Pidilite's FY25/FY26 results notes B2B underlying volume growth driven by both domestic and export segments, and international-subsidiary revenue (Asia, Middle East/Africa) growing mid-single digits; exports later described as 'struggling' amid geopolitical headwinds in FY26. No China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is in a net cash position (net debt approx. -Rs 123.5 Cr as of Mar-2025, improved from -Rs 446.7 Cr a year earlier; debt-to-equity ~1.5%), per balance-sheet aggregators citing FY25 filings, so interest-rate sensitivity is not a material disclosed risk.

crude_exposure.evidence: Analyst/press commentary (Business Standard and others, citing company disclosures) states VAM (vinyl acetate monomer, a crude-oil derivative largely imported) has historically constituted roughly 60% of Pidilite's raw material cost, with resins and other crude derivatives also material inputs.

inr_exposure.evidence: VAM is largely procured via imports (implying USD-denominated input costs), but no specific hedging policy or USD revenue percentage was found in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Coverage of ABB India's Integrated Annual Report/CY2024 results states ABB India 'is benefiting from the China+1 strategy' and is 'bullish on its export footprint expansion,' with export markets (esp. Distribution Solutions) cited alongside data-center order execution as growth drivers; the CEO separately described India becoming an export hub to support other ABB geographies (Business Today, Jan 2025).

govt_capex.evidence: AR/press commentary: order backlog of Rs 9,380 Cr (+12% YoY) at Dec-2024, with large orders +20% driven by data centers and railways; MD&A cites higher capex in infrastructure, railways, renewables, power distribution, water, energy and metals, plus PLI-led capex (specialty steel, battery manufacturing) as opportunity drivers. No specific revenue % tied to government/infra was disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABB India is in a large net-cash position (net debt approx. -Rs 10,966 Cr as of Dec-2024) and is described as 'almost debt free,' so interest-rate sensitivity is not material.

inr_exposure.evidence: India cited as contributing roughly 10-11% of ABB Group's global exports and serving 30+ export countries, but no ABB-India-specific USD revenue percentage or hedging policy was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: AR/press commentary frames PLI-led capex (e.g., specialty steel, battery manufacturing) as a demand tailwind for ABB India's customers/end-markets, not as ABB India itself receiving PLI incentive payouts. No confirmation found that ABB India is a direct PLI scheme beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company exports to 30+ countries and imports/distributes Diageo Scotch brands (Johnnie Walker, Lagavulin, Talisker) domestically, but no China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative was found; exports appear immaterial relative to the large domestic IMFL business.

rate_sensitive.evidence: FY25 aggregator data shows total debt of ~Rs 520 Cr against cash/short-term investments of ~Rs 2,100 Cr (net cash), debt-to-equity ~6.8%, and interest coverage of 25.0x (down slightly from 25.4x in FY24) -- indicating low overall debt but no floating-rate breakdown disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA, grain/molasses-based, not petrochemical) and glass are cited as USL's key raw materials, with ENA roughly 40% of raw material cost per market commentary; no crude/petrochemical (e.g., PET packaging) cost percentage was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative attributable to Sun Pharma found in sources reviewed (primary MD&A PDF fetch blocked, HTTP 403).

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 segment mix per press releases/earnings summaries: US ~31% of consolidated revenue (US formulation sales Rs 16,240 crore, +5.8%), India (domestic) formulation sales Rs 16,923 crore (+13.7%, ~31% of gross sales of Rs 52,041 crore), Emerging Markets ~18%, Global Specialty ~20%. Segments overlap in reporting so exact reconciliation to 100% not confirmed; primary AR MD&A PDF fetch blocked (403).

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma is cited as a qualifying beneficiary of the Rs 15,000 crore pharma PLI scheme, leveraged to expand critical API manufacturing capacity; no specific incentive/revenue amount disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Business is almost entirely domestic-focused; one quarterly commentary noted exports growth of 35.6% off a small base, but no China+1/diversification narrative or meaningful export revenue base was found.

rural.evidence: Press/analyst commentary describes Nestle India's 'RUrban' strategy expanding reach to ~216,000 villages (up from ~68,578 in CY20), with rural contribution estimated at roughly 20-25% of sales and a 26.6% 3-year rural sales CAGR versus 10.9% overall CAGR.

china_plus_one.evidence: Integrated Report 2024-25 discusses US-China trade tensions and policies like the proposed US Biosecure Act reducing dependency on China, prompting global pharma diversification toward regional manufacturing hubs, and positions Lupin's India-based manufacturing/CDMO operations as well-placed to support this shift. Narrative is contextual/strategic positioning rather than an explicit attribution of specific revenue/order growth to China+1, hence 'moderate' not 'strong'.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Lupin is exposed to USD-INR, EUR-INR and ZAR-INR movements across 100+ markets; treasury deploys a mix of natural hedges and forex derivatives with active, layered hedging monitored by treasury operations, though extreme currency moves can still affect profitability.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix (Integrated Report 2024-25 / Q4FY25 disclosures): India 34% (+14% YoY), US 38% (+16% YoY), EMEA 11% (+22% YoY), Growth Markets 9% (+7% YoY), API business ~5% of revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin is listed as a Category 1 PLI Pharma applicant (formulations PLI scheme) via its Aurangabad and Ankleshwar plants, qualifying as an integrated formulator with a complex-generics pipeline; no specific revenue/incentive amount disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company export sales contribute 6.56% of total turnover, with presence in 100+ countries and 35+ travel-retail locations, but no China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative was found in available sources.

rural.evidence: Commentary describes Radico as maintaining strong semi-urban and rural penetration (60,000+ retail outlets, pan-India network) alongside premiumization in urban markets, but no specific rural revenue percentage was disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt of ~Rs 737 Cr at FY2023-24 end (debt-to-equity ~0.3x); company targets becoming debt-free by FY2026 as major distillery capex (Rampur dual-feed, Sitapur greenfield, ~Rs 923 Cr since Apr-2022) winds down. No floating-vs-fixed rate breakdown found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Radico operates its own PET bottle manufacturing division (in-house packaging), and press commentary notes surging crude oil prices and a weaker rupee raising import costs for packaging/other inputs; no specific % of raw material cost tied to crude/PET was disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Government ethanol-blending policy is cited as tightening molasses availability and pushing Radico toward grain-based distilleries (new Sitapur greenfield plant), but this reflects an ethanol/biofuel policy tailwind, not confirmed PLI scheme incentive receipt.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sona Comstar draws >50% of sales from international markets across India, North America, Europe and Asia, with 12 manufacturing/assembly facilities across India, USA, Mexico and China. Company is pivoting toward Eastern markets and cited by a 2023 BCG study as a beneficiary of India's 'friend-shoring' positioning; separately it is India's largest importer of rare-earth magnets from China and is building domestic rare-earth-free motor and magnet manufacturing to de-risk that input dependency. No explicit 'China+1' framing with direct revenue/order attribution was found in AR-level text (sourced via news/investor-presentation coverage, not the AR itself).

inr_exposure.evidence: Company describes itself as deriving the majority of revenue from international (largely USD/EUR-billed) OEM customers in North America and Europe, but a precise USD-revenue % and formal hedging policy were not located within the fetch budget.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first Indian auto-component supplier to receive certification under the government's Auto PLI (Production-Linked Incentive) scheme, initially for a hub-wheel drive motor for electric two-wheelers, later adding certification for three more EV traction motor products (two for e-3-wheelers, one for e-2-wheelers). Company/management characterize Auto PLI as a margin/growth tailwind; exact revenue contribution not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Garware exports to 90+ countries with a large North America (largest single market) concentration, but no explicit 'China+1' or supply-chain-diversification narrative tied to revenue/order growth was found. The only China-linked disclosure found is a petition/expectation of benefit from an anti-dumping duty on TPU film imports FROM China into India (a domestic-market protection issue, not an export-diversification-away-from-China narrative).

crude_exposure.evidence: Major raw materials are PTA (Purified Terephthalic Acid) and MEG (Mono-ethylene Glycol), both petrochemical/crude-oil derivatives whose prices track crude; general polyester-industry estimates put PTA+MEG at >60% of production cost, but a Garware-specific raw-material % was not found. Company is backward-integrated into PET-chip manufacturing and sources RM at import-parity pricing from Indian refiners (e.g., Reliance), using forward contracts/long-term agreements to manage volatility.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Uses forward contracts and long-term supply agreements to manage raw-material/FX cost volatility (per secondary industry commentary); no formal hedging % disclosed in sources reviewed.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were ~77% of FY25 gross sales (up from 67% in FY23), with North America cited as the largest export market; precise USD-denominated revenue % not disclosed in sources reviewed.

govt_capex.evidence: Company explicitly cites government-led infrastructure development (railways, roads, gas pipelines, urban housing), railway modernization and defence-sector demand as growth drivers for its steel/stainless-steel/ferro-alloys business; has added dedicated railway sidings/lines at its Pandloi (Odisha) plant and is targeting ~$1bn revenue from its stainless-steel business (post Mittal Corp acquisition) partly on railway/infra/defence demand. No specific % of revenue tied to government/infra spend is disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company carries a conservatively low debt load (debt-to-equity roughly ~9%, total debt ~Rs 10.9bn vs equity ~Rs 118.6bn in FY25), suggesting limited overall rate sensitivity, but no floating-rate % of debt was disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Shyam Metalics Flat Products was selected as a beneficiary under the Government of India's ~Rs 6,322-crore PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel (covering categories including high-strength/wear-resistant steel and CRGO electrical steel used in automotive/power applications). Revenue contribution from PLI-linked capacity not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL maintained a near-debt-free consolidated balance sheet in FY25 (management describes 'nil net debt' and strong free cash flow); consolidated long-term borrowings fell to Rs 224.70 crore as of Mar-2025 from Rs 260.49 crore a year earlier, implying low overall interest-rate sensitivity, but no floating-rate % of debt is disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: IHCL's international hotel portfolio (Taj/Vivanta/Gateway/Ginger/SeleQtions brands) spans ~14-15 countries and contributes roughly 10-11% of operations (management states ~90% of the portfolio remains centered in the Indian subcontinent; international operations contributed ~11% of RevPAR growth in a recent quarter). FY25 standalone (largely domestic) revenue was Rs 5,145 crore vs consolidated Rs 8,565 crore. FY25 reported foreign-exchange earnings of Rs 733.28 crore vs outgo of Rs 81.65 crore, but no formal USD-revenue % or hedging policy was found.

FY25 segmental revenue: Domestic Rs2,269cr, International (formulations) Rs1,128cr, CDMO Rs446cr, API Rs76cr on total ~Rs3,918cr, giving domestic ~57.9% and combined export-oriented segments (International+CDMO+API) ~42.1%. Key export markets are Russia/CIS and South Africa (via subsidiaries) plus branded generics/CDMO exports across 40+ markets, implying multi-currency (not purely USD) exposure. Source: Q4FY25 result-update commentary summarizing AR/investor presentation segmental data.

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/analyst commentary (HDFC Sec deep-dive, Jan 2026) notes India's fluorochemicals and pharma/agrochem outsourcing sectors benefiting from global manufacturers diversifying supply chains beyond China; NFIL's CDMO business counts most of the top-20 global innovators as clients with multi-year, deep-integration contracts. No explicit 'China+1' phrase found directly quoted from the AR itself, so rated moderate rather than strong.

crude_exposure.evidence: Directors' Report/MD&A raw-material commentary: fluorspar prices rose over the year while sulphur, caustic soda and chloroform fell 51.3%/39.5%/46.1% YoY respectively; average natural gas price was ~16.76% lower YoY (natural gas/petrochemical-linked input). No explicit % of raw material cost tied to crude oil/petrochemical feedstock was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export contribution was reported at 77% of revenue in Q4FY25 (quarterly, not full-year figure), implying meaningful USD/foreign-currency exposure given global CDMO/specialty chemicals client base; no explicit hedging policy text located.

FY25 revenue by region: North America (Americas) ~53.9%, EMEA ~34.7%, remainder (~11.4%, APAC/RoW incl. India) per FY25 results commentary. As a US$1.45bn IT services exporter, the large majority of billing is in USD/GBP/EUR, but an explicit USD-denominated-revenue % and hedging/forward-contract policy text could not be located within the fetch budget (IR site and AR PDF returned 403).

rural.evidence: FY25 city-wise/class-wise domestic sales mix: Metro 34%, Town Class 1 23%, Town Class 2-6 23%, Rural 19% (per AR/investor materials). Combined Town Class 2-6 + Rural (i.e., smaller towns and rural markets together) is ~42% of domestic sales, above the Indian Pharma Market average, reflecting Mankind's tier-2/3/rural distribution strength.
